stem: Suppose a counselor records whether each of 200 students plays a school sport and whether the student usually gets at least 8 hours of sleep on a school night.\par\smallskip \textbf{Kai:} \emph{Seventy-five nonathletes but only 35 athletes get at least 8 hours, so playing a sport goes with less sleep.}\par \textbf{Rosa:} \emph{Those counts compare groups of different sizes; 35 out of 50 may tell a different story from 75 out of 150.}
first_take: Which student's reasoning seems more useful for deciding whether sport participation and sleep are related? Name one table detail.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the percent who get at least 8 hours of sleep in each sport group. Show the two fractions.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Whose reasoning is better supported? Use both percentages and explain why comparing 75 with 35 can mislead. State whether this table shows that playing a sport causes more sleep. Write 3--4 sentences.

answers.a: The variables are school-sport participation and usual school-night sleep category.
answers.c: Rosa's reasoning is supported: $70\%$ of athletes versus $50\%$ of nonathletes get at least 8 hours. The count 75 comes from a group of 150, three times the athlete group of 50, so the larger count does not mean a larger within-group percentage. The table shows an association for these students, but observing their choices does not show that playing a sport caused more sleep.

expectedElements.description: Supports Rosa using 70 percent versus 50 percent
Explains that unequal group totals make 75 versus 35 misleading
Limits the result to association, with no demonstrated cause

scoringGuide.E: Includes all three required reasoning elements above, with correct contextual evidence.
scoringGuide.P: Includes at least one substantive correct reasoning link above, but omits or misstates another required element.
scoringGuide.I: Includes no substantive correct reasoning link above; an unsupported choice or copied number alone is insufficient.

commonMistakes: Dividing 35 and 75 by the grand total instead of their row totals
Saying 75 is a larger percentage because it is a larger count
Claiming that association proves playing a sport increases sleep
